ratings_why.fun: Every recruit phase is a drag-then-buff puzzle with real choices about whom to climb, held back from 8 by heavy rule load, dead shop spells and a thin mono-tribe start.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the Climbers grow only by copying a host, so the tribe lives off the lobby: it hangs on Oozes, Hunters or a Pass target, and Cousin Dodder even copies the enemy's fight buffs. No tribe today plays like that.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken and the open questions are rulings for the owner; another pass would mostly shuffle numbers on a rule that already works.

points.text: Ruin Ivy turns every stray buff (a Pass, Harvest Supper, a neutral's spray) into a hub gain that all its Climbers then copy. That is the tribe's best hidden combo, so give the tribe bonus case a written ruling and let builds lean on it.
Let the player choose which Climber on Ivy in Flower Blooms, not always the biggest. A Bloomed unit gets Hold 1 and becomes a new host, so picking who comes out next is a real decision.

Missel saves Climbers from falling and Old Man's Beard feeds on falls, yet the Gatecrashers build lists both. Either count a Missel catch as a fall for Beard, or keep the tension and drop Missel from that build's list.
With Hold 1, Hazel Wand only ever gets +1 Health a turn. Make it 'whenever a Climber climbs this, give this +1/+1' so it rewards the re-hanging the tribe is built around.
Most cards point inward at Patrons. One more card at Tier 2 or 3 that pays off climbing another tribe's unit would make the Hangers-on build reachable before Midwinter Belle and Lady Hedera.

standouts.why: Viscum turns separate hosts into one web: every buff anywhere reaches every hosted Climber, so where you hang things matters across the whole board.
Ruin Ivy breaks the tribe's own rule in a way that makes outside buffs into hub multipliers.
Cousin Dodder points the rule at the enemy: he copies their fight buffs, and their biggest unit dying pays you.

weakest.why: Hazel Wand is +1 Health a turn with no decision attached.
Barley-Sugar Twiner does one obvious in-fight job and touches no other card.
Midwinter Belle is a one-off buff that is small on a mono board, and nothing else in the tribe cares how many tribes you run.

flags.note: Ruin Ivy (golden doubles it) with Harvest Supper or Pass funnels every Climber's share into one hub, and then all of them copy it. Worth a sim.
A golden Grand Oak with Hop Bine and Viscum stacks multipliers; the design already marks it as a high roll.
Several Honeysuckle Flatterers on one big Hold-3 or Hold-4 host give 3 to 4 gold a turn from a Tier 2 card.
Does Cousin Dodder stay in his own slot while he climbs an enemy that isn't next to him, and can his own side's attackers or effects still hit him?
When Missel catches Climbers that aren't next to him, do they keep their slots? 'Room or not' covers Hold but not being next to him.
